A small tree grows in a crack of the rock, and its roots make the crack wider. Yaya wonders how such a hard rock can crack and peel.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?

Name two things that damage the rock in the situation.
The heat of the sun and the roots of the tree damage the rock.
How can people protect a house against roots?
They should not plant big trees too close to walls and should remove young plants that grow in cracks.

qa.a: Physical weathering is the breaking of rocks into smaller pieces by physical forces, without any change in their minerals.

qa.q: Study the processes of physical weathering.

sum.title: I. Definition
defs: Physical (mechanical) weathering is the breaking of rocks into smaller pieces by physical forces, without any change in their chemical composition.

qa.q: Explain thermal shattering (exfoliation). What does it produce?
qa.a: By day, the outer layer of the rock heats and expands; at night, it cools and contracts. After many years, the outer layers crack and peel off. This forms curved sheets, rounded boulders and domes.

qa.q: Explain frost shattering. Where does it happen?
qa.a: Water in cracks freezes and expands by about 9%. The ice widens the cracks until the rock breaks. It happens in cold climates and high mountains, and it forms angular pieces called scree.

qa.q: Why do clay rocks on the banks of the Benue crumble?
qa.a: Clay rocks swell when wet and shrink when dry. This repeated wetting and drying (slaking) makes them crack and crumble.

qa.q: What happens when the rocks above a granite mass are removed by erosion?
qa.a: The pressure is released, the granite expands and cracks in sheets parallel to the surface. This is pressure release (unloading).

qa.q: How can plants and animals break rocks?
qa.a: Roots grow in cracks and widen them. Burrowing animals, such as termites and rodents, break and move rock pieces.

sum.title: II. Processes and Products of Physical Weathering
sum.intro: The main processes of physical weathering are the following:
items: Heating by day and cooling at night make the outer layers expand, contract and peel off. Products: curved sheets, rounded boulders and domes.
Water freezes in cracks and expands by about 9%, which widens the cracks. Product: angular pieces of rock (scree). It happens in cold regions.
Clay rocks swell when wet and shrink when dry, then crack and crumble. Product: small flakes of rock (banks of the Benue).
When the rocks above are removed, deep rocks such as granite expand and crack in sheets. Products: sheet joints and domes.
Roots widen cracks, and burrowing animals break and move rock pieces. Products: broken blocks and loose material.

evaluation: It is the cracking and peeling of rocks caused by heating by day and cooling at night.
Why is frost shattering rare in Garoua?
It is rare because temperatures in Garoua do not fall below 0 °C.
Roots grow in cracks, become thicker and widen the cracks until the rock breaks.
remediation: Peeling of rocks in layers is called ______.
Water expands by about ______ % when it freezes.
Angular rock pieces from frost shattering are called ______.
Wetting and drying of clay rocks is called ______.
end.homework: Look at an old iron gate, a roofing sheet or a nail left in the rain. Write what happened to it and what colour it became.
end.homeworkTag: This prepares Lesson 17: Chemical Weathering Processes and Products.
teacherNote: Correction: the source notes say that exfoliation produces inselbergs. Exfoliation produces curved sheets, rounded boulders and domes. Inselbergs are isolated hills formed by long weathering and erosion (Lesson 27); exfoliation can shape them, but does not form them alone.
Frost shattering: water expands by about 9% when it freezes.
